## 2. Budget Configuration — `page.budget-configuration`

**documentedBasis: none. coverageGuess: thin. uiVariant: undifferentiated. navPathEvidence: EMPTY. Zero fields is the correct answer.**

### The honest finding
There is **no Budget Configuration page in this corpus**. Exhaustive searches returned zero hits for every one of:
`Budget Configuration`, `budgetConfiguration`, `Budget Admin`, `Budget Item`, `Budget Manager`, `Budget Viewer`,
`Budget Owner`, `Budget Category`, `Manage Budget` — across both guide directories **and** both release-note
directories. There is no documented click path, no tab, no field, no role gate for such a page.

### What the corpus does instead
Every substantive Budget statement defers to an external guide that is not in this corpus:

> "For more information about budget approval and budget workflows, refer to the _Shared: Budget Setup Guide_."
> — admin/budget-approval-59251c3b.md

The same deferral appears in `approver-terminology-8559861c.md` (Budget Approver) and in both copies of
`add-a-custom-audit-rule-*.md` ("For audit rule notifications for Budget, refer to the Shared: Budget Setup Guide.").
The **Shared: Budget Setup Guide** is the named external authority. This corpus is Concur Invoice Professional
Edition only and does not contain it.

The remaining Budget mentions belong to OTHER, already-built pages and must not be re-homed here:
- **Audit Rules** (already built): `the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md` lists a *Budget* data object with Budget Amount,
  Budget Name, Budget Remaining Amount, Budget Type, HasBudget. These are audit-rule condition operands, not
  fields on a budget-configuration screen.
- **Workflows** (not yet built): `events-triggers-72339a13.md` documents a *Payment Request Budget Submit* event.
- Terminology only: *Budget Approver* in `approver-terminology-8559861c.md`; *Budget Center* as an example
  accounting segment in `define-the-who-in-a-transaction-1488d041.md`.
- One provisioning fact worth keeping: "The Budget feature is a purchased service."
  (`vat-at-the-line-item-level-itemization-summary-only-a41e7ad6.md`) — which explains the absence: Budget is a
  separately-purchased shared service documented outside the Invoice Professional Edition set.

**Recommendation:** either omit the page node entirely, or keep it as an explicit zero-field "documented
elsewhere" marker pointing at the Shared: Budget Setup Guide. Do not synthesise a screen.

## 3. List Management — `page.list-management`

**documentedBasis: sparse. coverageGuess: partial. uiVariant: undifferentiated.**

### Existence
Named as a page in three separate procedures, each ending "The List Management page appears."

### Distinct documented click paths (3)
| # | Path | File |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Administration > Invoice > List Management | admin/use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md — "1.  Select Administration\>Invoice." then "2.  Select List Management (left menu). The List Management page appears." |
| 2 | Administration > Invoice > List Management | admin/use-a-connected-list-1eaafd29.md — "2.  Select List Management (left menu). The List Management page appears." |
| 3 | Administration > Invoice > List Management | tools/step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md — "2.  Click List Management (left menu). The List Management page appears." |

**TEXT TRAP — non-breaking spaces.** The step-1 lines of paths 2 and 3 are NOT plain ASCII:
`1.  Select Administration␠U+00A0␠U+00A0␠Invoice .` and `1.  Click Administration␠U+00A0␠U+00A0␠Invoice.`
Path 1's step 1 is `1.  Select Administration\>Invoice.` — the "Administration >Invoice" no-space trap, with a
markdown-escaped `\>`. Only path 1's step-1 line is safely quotable; for paths 2 and 3 the second step is quoted
instead. Do not "clean up" these strings.

### PAGE IDENTITY — List Management vs the Connected Lists tab (RESOLVED, with one contradiction)
The corpus **does** separate them, and they must stay separate:

- **Connected Lists is a TAB on the already-built Forms and Fields page.**
  "1.  On the Forms and Fields page, in the Form Type list, select the desired form type." /
  "2.  Click the Connected Lists tab." (admin/access-connected-lists-39dd2408.md)
  "You can use the Connected Lists tab to add new connected list definitions and modify existing connected list
  definitions." (admin/connected-list-overview-3fc65ecf.md)
  "The Connected Lists tab is available only when you select a form that supports this feature; otherwise, it is
  disabled." (admin/work-with-connected-list-definitions-4dd05e1d.md)
  → All connected-list DEFINITION controls (Select a List / Select fields / Configure User Interface / Preview /
  Assign to Forms) belong to `page.forms-and-fields`, field `connectedListsTab`. Do NOT re-home them.

- **List Management holds the list CATEGORY, the list, and the list ITEMS.**
  "Using the combination of the List Management and Forms and Fields tools, the administrator can create a
  connected list whose first field is an expense type." (admin/use-an-expense-type-as-the-first-field-in-a-connected-list-e0c5f415.md)
  "You use the Forms and Fields and List Management pages to perform the following tasks, typically in the order
  shown." + "On the List Management page:" (admin/forms-fields-lists-and-validations-configuration-process-76d94b3b.md)
  "In List Management, you create the source list associated with the feature hierarchies." (admin/overview-8b2edfd0.md)

- **CONTRADICTION (ownership of connected-list definitions).** One topic attributes the definition work to a
  third, differently-named tool owned by a different role:
  "Shared Configuration administrator: Using the Connected List Definition tool to define the connected list
  fields and hierarchy" (admin/use-a-connected-list-1eaafd29.md)
  versus access-connected-lists-39dd2408.md placing exactly that work on the Forms and Fields > Connected Lists
  tab. Recorded, not reconciled. Plausibly provisioning-dependent (Shared Configuration is a cross-product tool),
  but the corpus does not say so and I will not infer it.

### Controls actually documented (why "sparse")
Only a short procedure's worth: **New** button → **New List** page → **List Name**, choose an existing list
category or **New List Category** / **Add New List Category**, **Save**; then per-item **Item Code**,
**Save and Add**, **Done**. There is no field table for the List Management page anywhere in the corpus.
Everything else is deferred outward — and the deferral target is itself inconsistently named:
- "refer to the Shared: List Management Setup Guide." (admin/use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md, and 6 more topics)
- "refer to _Concur Invoice: List Management Setup Guide_." (tools/step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md)
Neither guide is in this corpus. **CONTRADICTION (external source name)** recorded.

### Aliases
"List Management tool", "List Management page", "Step 1: List Management" (tools/overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md).

### Role gates — CONTRADICTION (three different roles)
- **Invoice Admin** — "This portion of the process requires the role of Invoice Admin." (admin/use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md)
- **Invoice Admin + Shared Configuration administrator** — "This portion of the process requires the roles of
  Invoice Admin and Shared Configuration administrator." (admin/use-a-connected-list-1eaafd29.md) — but the
  Shared Configuration half is scoped to the Connected List Definition tool, not to List Management itself.
- **Invoice Configuration Administrator** — "Invoice Configuration Administrator: Will configure the Concur
  Invoice modules, such as List Management, Group Configurations, and Employee form" (tools/required-roles-53a9a79c.md);
  reinforced by tools/overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md: "All tasks require the Invoice Configuration administrator
  role unless".
All three recorded. The corpus gives no single answer.

## Cross-cutting observations

1. **Two competing top-level menu labels.** Three of the four pages have at least one path rooted at
   "Invoice Admin" rather than "Administration > Invoice" (Tax Administration, Company Locations). The alias is
   live and must be tried by the click-path resolver.
2. **"Invoice Processing Admin" coverage is uneven.** It is asserted for Company Locations only. Tax
   Administration and List Management are documented purely as "(left menu)" items after Administration > Invoice.
   Do not assume the middle node for them; there is no quote for it.
3. **Non-breaking spaces are a real hazard** in the List Management nav lines and would silently break a
   `grep -F` validation if copied naively.
4. **Gerund/imperative twins** confirmed for the tax predefined-tax-code procedure
   (`configure-predefined-tax-codes-6b42509f.md` "Select" vs `step-7-...-be8bc5b8.md` "Click"). Same
   `deliverable_id: 41460672`, same content, NOT a UI variant.
5. **No UI-variant evidence at all** for any of the four pages — no NextGen/legacy language anywhere. All four
   are `undifferentiated`.
6. **One of the four pages should probably not exist.** Budget Configuration has zero documentary basis. That is
   the finding, not a gap to be filled.

### Census-method warning for the extraction agents
`grep -c '^|'` **undercounts badly** in this corpus. SAP tables inside numbered procedure steps are
indented four spaces, so the anchor must be `grep -cE '^ *\|'`. Example:
`T/add-a-shipping-or-billing-address-3b51c816.md` scores `^|` = 0 but `^ *\|` = 39 and in fact holds a
**12-row field catalog**. If an extractor uses `^|` it will declare that file table-free and lose the
entire Company Locations field set.

fields.name: shipToTab
fields.label: Ship To
fields.sourceQuote: On the Company Locations page, select the Ship To tab.
fields.notes: Tab control on the Company Locations page; every action on the page (New / Modify / Remove / Import / Export All) is scoped to the selected tab. REPAIRED IN MERGE: the crosscut lens typed this 'button'; set to 'unknown', the graph's settled convention for tabs (capture_processing_admin_tabs, scanConfigurationsTab, imagingTabSelector, validationsTab, connectedListsTab) - the corpus says only 'tab' and never states the widget category. Corroborated in admin-guides: 'Add one or more shipping addresses by clicking Ship To and then New.' (concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md).

fields.name: billToTab
fields.label: Bill To
fields.sourceQuote: On the Company Locations page, select the Ship To or Bill To tab.
fields.notes: Second tab, named alongside Ship To in the delete and export procedures ('On the Company Locations page, select the Ship To or Bill To tab.'). REPAIRED IN MERGE: the crosscut lens typed this 'button'; set to 'unknown' per the graph's tab convention. The per-tab field set is NOT identical: VAT ID is documented as 'This is only applicable on the bill-to address and required by some European countries.' The corpus never names an 'Add New Bill To Location' window - the 12-row field table is written from the ship-to path with bill-to-only annotations.

fields.name: newButton
fields.label: New
fields.sourceQuote: Select New to open the Add New Ship To Location window.
fields.notes: Opens the Add New Ship To Location window (per admin-guides, also invoked for adding a bill-to address: 'Add one or more shipping addresses by clicking Ship To and then New.'). Role gate (tool-wide): requires Invoice Configuration administrator or Invoice Configuration (Restricted) administrator role (required-roles-476a5f62.md).

fields.name: modifyButton
fields.label: Modify
fields.sourceQuote: Select the address and select Modify
fields.notes: Two documented paths to the same modal: select the row then Modify, or 'Double-click the address directly'. Opens the Modify Ship To Location window. Addresses that arrived via the Purchase Order import are editable here too: 'You can edit shipping and billing addresses that were created in Company Locations or imported through the Purchase Order import.'

fields.name: removeButton
fields.label: Remove
fields.sourceQuote: Select Remove. The following confirmation message appears:
fields.notes: Supports selecting one or more addresses first ('Select the address or addresses.'). Deletion is a soft delete: 'The address remains available and can be reactivated by entering the same Address Code. The system creates a new record.'

fields.name: removeConfirmYesButton
fields.label: Yes
fields.sourceQuote: Select Yes to remove the address from the Company Locations page.
fields.notes: Confirms the 'Remove selected Company Locations' confirmation dialog raised by the Remove button.

fields.name: importButton
fields.label: Import
fields.sourceQuote: Select the Import button. The Import Ship To Locations window appears.
fields.notes: Opens the Import Ship To Locations window. Distinct from importSubmitButton, the in-window button that actually performs the import.

fields.name: downloadImportTemplateLink
fields.label: Download the import template
fields.sourceQuote: Select Download the import template link if you want to download a template with the field names already filled in.
fields.notes: PUBLISHABLE DOCUMENTED GAP: the template's COLUMN LIST is nowhere in this corpus. The topic says only that the template arrives with 'the field names already filled in' and never enumerates them. The nearest documented column set is the Purchase Order import 210/220 record format, which is a DIFFERENT import - see contradictions. The Country Code row of the add-address table is the one hint that the template and the UI share fields ('If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.').

fields.name: browseButton
fields.label: Browse
fields.sourceQuote: Select Browse and locate the file that you want to import.
fields.notes: Opens a file picker; the next step ('Select the file and then select Open.') is the OS file-open dialog, not a Concur Invoice control, but is recorded as an admin-facing step in the numbered procedure.

fields.name: openButton
fields.label: Open
fields.sourceQuote: Select the file and then select Open.
fields.notes: SCOPE FLAG (first-class, not prose): this is the OPERATING-SYSTEM file chooser's Open button, NOT a control rendered by companyLocations.asp. It is retained because it is a verbatim-grounded step of the page's numbered import procedure ('Select Browse and locate the file that you want to import.' then 'Select the file and then select Open.'), but a Chromium automation must set the file input directly and will never see this dialog - do not treat it as a page element or a wait target. REFUTER SPLIT: refuter 1 kept it (the record already declared its own scope); refuter 2 would have dropped it as an OS control, citing page.routing-configuration, which records Browse and Download Template but deliberately records no Open. Repaired rather than deleted because this roster has no configSteps array to demote it into, so dropping would lose the documented step entirely.

fields.name: importSubmitButton
fields.label: Import
fields.sourceQuote: Select Import.
fields.notes: The in-window submit control of the Import Ship To Locations window (distinct from importButton, which only opens that window). Produces the Import Summary page.

fields.name: importSummaryCloseButton
fields.label: Close
fields.sourceQuote: Click Close.
fields.notes: Closes the Import Summary page. After closing, status appears in the 'Ship To Locations import history' section of the Import Ship To Locations page.

fields.name: exportAllButton
fields.label: Export All
fields.sourceQuote: Select the Export All button.
fields.notes: Available on both the Ship To and Bill To tabs ('select the Ship To or Bill To tab' precedes this step); produces an Excel spreadsheet of all addresses on the selected tab.

fields.name: saveButton
fields.label: Save
fields.sourceQuote: Select Save to enter the new address into Concur Invoice.
fields.notes: Same control also documented in the edit procedure with the shorter phrasing 'Select Save.' (edit-a-shipping-or-billing-address-c8138913.md), used to commit the Add New / Modify Ship To Location window.

fields.name: removeConfirmation
fields.label: Remove selected Company Locations (confirmation message)
fields.sourceQuote: Remove selected Company Locations
fields.notes: REPAIRED IN MERGE: this record was typed 'button' with the label 'Remove selected Company Locations', which asserts a clickable button carrying the text of a confirmation MESSAGE - an automation told to click a button by that name would fail. The corpus says 'Select Remove. The following confirmation message appears:' followed by that string, so fieldType is now 'unknown' (the graph has no dialog type) and the label states it is the message. Useful to a crawler only as proof the modal opened. The ONLY documented control inside the dialog is Yes ('Select Yes to remove the address from the Company Locations page.'), carried separately as removeConfirmYesButton - the two must not be merged. NO negative/Cancel control is documented anywhere in this corpus; that half of the pair must NOT be completed.

fields.name: locationName
fields.label: Name
fields.sourceQuote: A unique name that identifies a specific address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 1 of the 12-row 'Field / Description/Comments' table in the Add New Ship To Location window. Note in the same cell: 'This is the value that displays when choosing a default shipping address in Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Preferences, and when creating a policy and selecting the value for Bill To.' Tip in the same cell: 'The system searches for your location by using the Name value.' No length limit documented for this field on the page (the PO import 210/220 Name column is capped at 100 characters, but that is the import file, not the page).

fields.name: addressCode
fields.label: Address Code
fields.sourceQuote: This is the external identifier used by the customer's financial system to identify a specific address.
fields.notes: REQUIRED. The page's true identity key across three integrations: (1) 'This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.' and the PO import matches on it; (2) the Employee Import 360-record set assigns a user's default shipping address by Address Code; (3) Peppol matches inbound invoices on the ship-to address code. Re-entering a removed Address Code reactivates the address as a NEW record.

fields.name: address1
fields.label: Address 1
fields.sourceQuote: Address 1 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 3. No length limit documented for the on-page field (the PO import 210/220 column is 'Maximum 255 characters').

fields.name: address2
fields.label: Address 2
fields.sourceQuote: Address 2 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 4.

fields.name: address3
fields.label: Address 3
fields.sourceQuote: Address 3 of the complete address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 5.

fields.name: city
fields.label: City
fields.sourceQuote: The city within which the address resides.
fields.notes: Required. Row 6.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.label: Postal Code
fields.sourceQuote: The postal code of the address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 7.

fields.name: countryCode
fields.label: Country Code
fields.sourceQuote: The code of the country associated with the address.
fields.notes: Required. Row 8. Note in the same cell: 'If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.' The corpus does NOT enumerate the accepted values for this on-page field and does not point it at any list. The 249-row Country Code List catalog in country-code-list-8b3e2eda.md is documented for a different scope ('the country code list that you use when creating the vendor import file') and is therefore recorded as an UNWIRED value set, not as this field's validValues. fieldType left unknown: the corpus never states whether this is a text box or a list, and the guide revision history dated March 18, 2016 notes only that the State/Province field 'has changed to a list', not Country Code.

fields.name: stateProvince
fields.label: State/Province
fields.sourceQuote: The state or province within which the address resides.
fields.notes: Optional on the Company Locations page (row 9). CONTRADICTION with the PO import: both the 210 and 220 record formats mark State/Province Required? = Y. The guide revision history dates the page-side change: September 9, 2016 'State/Province field now an optional field', and March 18, 2016 'Updated images to show that the State/Province field has changed to a list when creating a new ship-to or bill-to address' — the list contents are never enumerated in this corpus, so validValues is empty and fieldType is left unknown rather than asserted as a dropdown.

fields.name: emailAddress
fields.label: Email Address
fields.sourceQuote: The email address of the contact at the company location.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 10. Added per the guide revision history dated April 14, 2018 ('the addition of the email address field to the add and modify ship-to and bill-to windows'). Consumed by the Purchase Order Header 'Use Email as Bill-To' field configured on Forms and Fields — see dependencyCandidates.

fields.name: vatId
fields.label: VAT ID
fields.sourceQuote: The VAT of the buyer.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 11. Note in the same cell: 'This is only applicable on the bill-to address and required by some European countries.' This is the row that makes the Ship To and Bill To tab field sets non-identical. Added per the guide revision history dated September 9, 2016 ('VAT ID field in bill-to address'). The corpus does not say which European countries make it required.

fields.name: addAddressAsShipToLocationAsWell
fields.label: Add address as a Ship To Location as well
fields.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box if you would like to populate the ship-to address with the same address information as the bill-to address.
fields.notes: Optional. Row 12, the last row of the table. Explicitly typed as a check box by the source ('this check box'), so 'checkbox' here is documented, not inferred. Functionally a bill-to-side control (it copies the bill-to address into a ship-to record), although the table it lives in is introduced under 'select the Ship To tab' — the corpus does not resolve that tension. No default state is documented; no on/off value labels are enumerated, so validValues stays empty.

pages.verifyNotes: REFUTER PAGE-LEVEL FINDINGS AND WHAT I DID ABOUT THEM. (1) GROUNDING: refuter-1 grep-verified all 25 distinct quote strings across the three extraction files and found zero quote defects (verbatimVariantIndex 0 everywhere; every variantSpellings array had exactly one entry). I re-ran grep -F -c independently on all 30 lens records, including every twin I did not emit: ALL returned 1. Every record in this roster was pulled programmatically out of the extraction JSON - no sourceQuote was retyped. No quote was hand-authored, so no new grounding risk was introduced. (2) RAW TABLES: grep -c '<table' on all four cited files (cc91aa73, f3fc8bee, 1eaafd29, e0c5f415) returns 0, so fromRawHtmlTable:false is correct on all 14 records and no false flag needed clearing. There is no page-relevant raw <table> file for List Management in either guide directory. (3) THE ONE TRUE REPAIR: newListCategoryOption carried fieldType 'radio' (procedures lens) vs 'dropdown' (crosscut lens), with the corpus supporting neither - the only sentence is 'Create New: Select New List Category and, in Add New List Category, type a name and select Save.' Repaired to 'unknown', and the underlying ambiguity (is New List Category a standalone control or an option value inside listCategory?) is RECORDED AS UNDETERMINED rather than resolved, with an explicit instruction that if it is ever established to be a value it must move into listCategory.validValues and this field must be removed, so the string is never counted twice. (4) THE INVENTED-VALUE CATCH: the tables lens's dropped twin listCategorySelector carried validValues ['New List Category'] plus a matching valueSetCandidate. I did NOT carry either forward. The corpus never states that the New List Category entry lives inside the category control; membership is plausible but unstated, which is exactly the completion class this project has already had to delete twice. RECOMMENDATION TO THE MERGER: DROP that value set outright rather than rewiring its appliesToField to listCategory - rewiring re-asserts the unproven membership. Every one of the 14 surviving records has validValues []. 'Allocations' (illustrative existing category), EAST/NORTH and the four Divisions (the guide's worked example), and AWRDS were all correctly kept out of validValues by all three lenses; I confirm those exclusions - they are tenant or example data, not documented system enumerations. (5) REFUTER DISAGREEMENTS I HAD TO SETTLE (both are duplicate pairs where each refuter kept the opposite twin, so both names arrived in the REPAIR bucket). newButton vs newListButton: kept newListButton, because field.exceptions.newButton already means a different control in the existing graph and this page carries a second New (listItemsNewButton) that the bare name does not disambiguate against. multiLevelSubLevel vs addSubLevels: kept addSubLevels, because it already carries the two findings refuter-1 asked to be folded forward (no documented depth limit on List Management; depth bounded only downstream by the compressed range Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code). Both losers are logged in dropped[] with duplicateOf. This is why 16 inputs yield 14 records: the two removals are intra-page duplicates of surviving controls, not lost surface. (6) FOLD-FORWARDS the refuters ordered before discarding duplicates, all done: listItemCode's 32-character import-column limit (with the caveat preserved that it is stated about the IMPORT COLUMN, not this entry field) and the import-allocations rule 'It is critical that import values be the list item code, and not the list item name (the display name) value.' into itemCode; listItemName's UNDETERMINED note into itemName; listCategorySelector's value-set warning into listCategory. I grep-verified the import-allocations sentence (present in admin-guides/import-allocations-5ca442db.md) before quoting it in a note. (7) VARIANT SELECTION: where a control was found by two lenses with different but equally verbatim quotes, I took the record whose notes carry more documented constraint, and for itemName I took refuter-1's explicit recommendation - the crosscut's full-sentence quote, so the conditional 'If the name is to appear the same for connected list audit rules' survives inside the quote itself rather than only in notes. (8) PAGE IDENTITY HELD, RE-CHECKED. Not one emitted record is a connected-list-DEFINITION control. e0c5f415 splits the work by tool in its own words - 'List Management: The connected list is configured using an expense type as the first field, with an Item Code that ...' versus 'Forms and Fields: The connected list created in List Management is chosen when defining the connected list' - and 39dd2408 places the Connected Lists tab on the Forms and Fields page. Nothing was re-homed here from page.forms-and-fields and nothing here belongs there. I checked the live graph (337 configFields): the ONLY name collision is field.exceptions.newButton, which is benign (ids are namespaced by page) and which I avoided anyway by keeping newListButton. RESIDUAL CONTRADICTION RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: use-a-connected-list-1eaafd29.md attributes definition work to a third, differently-named 'Connected List Definition tool' under the Shared Configuration administrator, which conflicts with 39dd2408 placing it on the Forms and Fields Connected Lists tab. No field was moved on the strength of either. (9) TWO CONTROLS FLAGGED BUT NOT ADDED. The category-level Save inside Add New List Category is a real, unmodelled third Save - reported in splitsProposed, not emitted, because records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter. 'Expense Type List Item Key' (e0c5f415, with hard constraints that it must be first in the connected list and is usable in only one definition) is almost certainly a connected-list DEFINITION field belonging to page.forms-and-fields; it is deliberately NOT homed here. (10) MUST-READ FILES: refuter-2 opened all 12; refuter-1 opened the 4 cited by candidates plus 4 more. For my own pass I re-read the two files that actually ground this roster in full - tools-guides/step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md and admin-guides/use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md - and confirmed the step sequence, the Note about the EAST; NORTH code format, and the 'make note of the category name and the list name' caveat. I did not re-open overview-8b2edfd0.md, step-2-...-bcaf1f5a.md, overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md, required-roles-53a9a79c.md, field-configuration-information-5813462a.md, additional-documentation-a105a5d7.md, access-connected-lists-39dd2408.md, 76d94b3b.md or e0c5f415.md at this stage: no repair I performed touches them, both refuters read them and reported consistently, and my lens here is assembly of already-refuted records rather than fresh extraction. See mustReadSkipped equivalent in this note. (11) COVERAGE = THIN, AND IT STAYS THIN. All three extraction lenses independently returned coverageVerdict 'thin' and both refuters affirmed it. The reason is not a failed search: grep -rl 'List Management' over BOTH guide directories returns exactly 20 files, 18 of which the extractions read and the remaining 2 (creating-and-approving-a-new-vendor-fa0ecc4e.md, vendor-manager-terminology-8b54bff7.md) yield no controls. There is NO field table, NO option catalog and NO raw <table> for this page anywhere in the corpus. use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md step 5 concedes the gap in the product's own documentation - 'Fill out the remaining options, then select Save.' - and nine topics defer the substance to an external 'Shared: List Management Setup Guide' (called 'Concur Invoice: List Management Setup Guide' in tools-guides/step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md) that is not in this corpus. The 14 controls here are a procedural skeleton: the nav link, the two New buttons, List Name, the category choice, the item fields, and the three terminal buttons. NOTHING WAS PADDED TO FILL THE GAP, and the automation must be told that the New List page has unnamed options it will encounter and cannot plan for. No record models that step and none should be hand-reconstructed; page.audit-rules models its equivalent, List Management deliberately does not.

pages.verifyNotes:
WHAT THE REFUTERS FOUND, AND WHAT I DID ABOUT IT.

1. GROUNDING WAS ALREADY CLEAN, AND I RE-PROVED IT. Both refuters ran a full mechanical sweep (142 / 145 variant records) and found 0 non-verbatim quotes, 0 missing files, 0 CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefixes, 0 false fromRawHtmlTable flags. I re-ran the same sweep myself with `grep -F -c` over all 98 candidate records before touching anything (0 failures), and re-ran it AGAIN over the 59 finished roster records after every repair (0 failures). Every sourceFile in this roster exists, is prefixed with its guide directory, and every one of them is in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/.

2. THE ONE THING THE REFUTERS DISAGREED ABOUT: NAMING. This was the whole substance of the pass. Refuter 1 (grounding) nominated the PROCEDURE-lens short prefixes (col* / tv* / etg* / vg*) as survivors of 36 duplicate pairs; refuter 2 (duplication) nominated the LONG-FORM names (taxAuthoritiesGrid* / taxValidation* / expenseTypeGroup* / vendorGroup*). Every pair cites the same sentence in the same file, so grounding could not break the tie and both refuters said so explicitly. I adopted refuter 2's long-form convention for the ENTIRE set, which is exactly the inversion refuter 1 authorised ('If refuter 2 nominates the long-form names instead, invert the whole set consistently - but NEVER delete both halves of a pair'). Reasons: (a) the three contradiction records (uniqueTaxPartnerNumber, requestTypeToBeAnalyzed, formLevelToBeAnalyzed) name taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber / taxValidationType / taxValidationLevel in their own notes, so surviving tv* would have broken three cross-references that now resolve; (b) colTaxAuthorityName is confusable with the wizard input taxAuthorityName (the grid column is labelled plain 'Tax Authority', the input 'Tax Authority Name'); (c) the long-form names are self-describing for a crawler and collide with nothing in the existing 337-field graph (I checked all 59 names against output/kg-invoice-config.json - zero exact collisions). NO PAIR LOST BOTH HALVES: 36 pairs in, 36 survivors out, and every dropped twin's better material was folded into its survivor.

3. WHERE THE DROPPED HALF WAS THE BETTER RECORD, I TOOK ITS CONTENT. That is the whole point of a three-way disposition. Nine quotes were replaced with the better-anchored or fuller sentence FROM THE SAME FILE and re-verified: taxAuthoritiesGridStateProvince, taxAuthoritiesGridTaxName, taxRateTaxPercent, taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber, taxValidationType, taxValidationExpenseTypes, expenseTypeGroupTaxCode, expenseTypeGroupRateTypeColumn, vendorGroupTaxCode, vendorGroupDisableVatCalculation. The single most important one is unspscCommodityCode, whose surviving spelling quoted 'A Search link is provided to open a browser to the latest UN commodity codes for accurate input.' - the description of the ADJACENT Search LINK. Left alone, unspscCommodityCode and unspscCommodityCodeSearch would have shipped with one identical sentence as the evidence for two different controls. Repaired with the sentence that actually defines the commodity code field.

4. VALUES: TWO STRIPPED, ONE FLAGGED, ZERO INVENTED. (a) expenseTypeGroupAppliesTo carried ['Payment Request'] and vendorGroupAppliesTo carried ['Payment request']; both STRIPPED to []. 'Select the Payment Request document type for which to calculate VAT...' is prose naming one document type, not an enumerated option list, and I confirmed by grep that 'Applies To' appears in exactly two tax files corpus-wide (step-5 and step-6) and is never enumerated in either. Two of the three lenses had already left it empty. The strings survive verbatim in the sourceQuotes, and the REAL finding - step-5 writes 'Payment Request', step-6 writes 'Payment request' - is recorded on both records and deliberately NOT normalised. (b) formLevelToBeAnalyzed keeps ['header','line item details form'] but they are now marked PROSE-DERIVED in the notes with an explicit instruction not to select an option literally named 'line item details form'; both refuters filed this and both accepted marking as sufficient. (c) The valueSet wired to taxAuthorityCountry - ['United Kingdom','Japan','Australia'] from supported-countries-for-vat-8b38bab8.md - is DETACHED and the detachment is stated in the field's notes; that sentence is VAT support scope, not the Country dropdown's options, and the corpus enumerates no country list anywhere. validValues on Country stays []. Nothing was added to any validValues array in this pass. taxRateTypeCalculationMethod still carries exactly one value ('Percentage', documented as the default) and no second method was invented; the two tax-condition records still carry exactly 'Always' and the notes say whether other conditions exist is UNDETERMINED.

5. FOUR TYPE/LABEL DEFECTS FIXED. expenseTypeGroupTaxCondition and vendorGroupTaxCondition both stored the VALUE 'Always' in the label slot with fieldType 'table'; both are now label '(tax condition)' / fieldType 'unknown', which is the honest form the procedure lens had used. taxValidationLevel is now fieldType 'unknown' because the corpus states no control type and the lenses guessed 'radio' and 'dropdown' respectively - an unstable inference does not belong in a graph a crawler will drive. taxAuthoritiesList had a stray foreign quote in its notes (the row text of taxAuthoritiesGridStateProvince); removed, and the record is now explicitly marked as the CONTAINER whose four columns are the taxAuthoritiesGrid* records, so the same grid is not represented five times as peer fields.

6. CONTRADICTIONS PRESERVED, NOT RECONCILED. Six live in this roster: the tab label ('Expense Type Groups' vs 'Expense Types Group'); the three Tax Validation label pairs (Partner Account Number / Unique Tax Partner Number, Tax Validation Type / Request Type to be Analyzed, Tax Validation Level / Form Level to Be Analyzed, the last also splitting on value spelling Header|Line Item vs header|line item details form); the Applies To casing; and the predefined-tax-code result ('the tax code fields (1-4)' in 6b42509f vs 'the VAT Tax Code 1 field' in be8bc5b8). The three alternate-label records SURVIVE as records - a naive de-duplication pass would have deleted them and erased the finding - but each now opens with an explicit 'ALIAS OF <name> - NOT a second control' cross-link so an automation fills ONE field and matches EITHER label. Also preserved untouched: the country-support contradiction (admin supported-countries-for-vat-8b38bab8.md says US/Canada/India are not supported; tools-guides canada-de22c9f9.md and uk-us-japan-australia-0557084a.md give full US and Canada VAT field implementations) and the lens disagreement over the 'with effective dates' parenthetical.

7. NO SPLITS EXECUTED. Five inputs are genuinely several controls - buttonNew (six New buttons), buttonSave (four), buttonNext (three wizards), buttonDone (three), buttonSearchGroups (two tabs). All five are reported in splitsProposed and NONE was split, because records created in Repair never face the adversarial refuter and 18 new unrefuted button nodes is exactly the failure this constraint exists to prevent. 95 names in, 59 out, no name invented.

8. NEGATIVE FINDINGS WORTH PUBLISHING. (a) 'withholding' returns ZERO files across both guide directories - withholding tax has no documentary basis in this corpus and no control was invented for it. (b) NO Modify / Edit / Remove / Delete control is documented anywhere for tax authorities, tax rate types, tax rates, tax codes, expense type groups or vendor groups - the page's entire edit/delete surface is undocumented, and refuter 1 confirmed this by searching the narrative topics. That is a real gap in the docs, not a gap in this roster. (c) tools-guides documents ZERO controls of this page; all 59 records cite admin-guides. Tax Administration is genuinely an admin-guides-only page and the citation ratio must not be forced - the tools-guides tax topics (canada-de22c9f9, uk-us-japan-australia-0557084a, other-countries-84722445, switch-tax-mode-dcd0a51d) are VAT FIELD and end-user topics, not controls here. (d) No country list, no state/province list, and no second Calculation Method is enumerated anywhere; [] on those fields is the correct answer, not thin coverage. (e) Switch Tax Mode is correctly ABSENT - the corpus places that button on the end-user Invoice page.

9. NOTHING WAS RE-HOMED ONTO THIS PAGE. The four long VAT catalogs (27-row available-vat-fields-8b395ce2, 12-row extract-vat-data-8b3996e0, 4-row configure-vat-labels-9d4795b9) are Forms-and-Fields form fields, the two OCR raw-<table> twins are Capture Processing Admin, vendor-tax-id-0f8f83bc is Audit Rules, and the digital tax invoice status list is Image Handling (where page.image-handling already carries digitalTaxInvoiceCfdiStatus). All were left with empty appliesToField by the extractors and refuter 2 verified by grep that not one of the 98 candidates belongs on another admin page. Zero drops for mis-assignment.

10. FILE THE INVENTORY MISSED. Refuter 2 found concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/the-basic-process-13c136d5.md, a SECOND 'The Basic Process' topic (different loio and different content from the-basic-process-12a5686d.md already in the inventory). It is the Tax Validation basic process; it corroborates taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber, turnOnTaxValidation (confirming the checkbox type) and the initial UNSPSC import, and states the provisioning gate in its own words. It contributes no new control, and it is now cited in the notes of the two records it corroborates.

MUST-READ FILES I DID NOT OPEN MYSELF, and why. My lens is assembly, and the two refuters between them read every must-read that any candidate cites and reported no unresolved defect in them. I opened or grepped: step-4-add-a-new-tax-authority-7f90cede, step-3-configure-the-service-14c3ef13, step-5-...-e8d87361, step-6-...-d8b7786d, step-3-access-tax-authorities-2fae4ae3, configure-predefined-tax-codes-6b42509f, work-with-the-tax-validation-page-options-c3fe1df5 and the-basic-process-12a5686d (every quote in this roster is greppable against them). I did NOT re-read: step-7-...-be8bc5b8, both step-2-assign-the-tax-administrator-role files, step-1-enable-the-tax-validation-feature-31fca0d8 (role and provisioning gates - Map-phase material, no field record depends on them); available-vat-fields-8b395ce2, extract-vat-data-8b3996e0, configure-vat-labels-9d4795b9, supported-countries-for-vat-8b38bab8, canada-de22c9f9, uk-us-japan-australia-0557084a, other-countries-84722445, switch-tax-mode-dcd0a51d, configure-the-specify-tax...-11c6df01, control-tax-amount-handling-8540cd38, step-3-optional-...-69ba75a6, understand-and-use-the-effective-date-...-ccf72f26, requirements-to-calculate-vat-821a71ea, calculate-vat-and-required-criteria-89f97622 (cross-cutting VAT, country, dependency and value-set material that supplies ZERO of the 59 roster records; both refuters verified that no candidate here is a VAT form field, a country row or a digital-tax-invoice status). Those files matter to the page's dependencies and value sets, which are not this roster's output.

COVERAGE: good. Five tabs, five action buttons, a fully enumerated 4-column grid, a 3-step 9-field New Tax Authority wizard, a 6-row Tax Validation table and two 6-row group wizards are all documented at field level, with every row present and none sampled. The honest gap is the undocumented edit/delete surface, which is a documentation gap rather than a coverage failure on my part.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: One sentence anywhere in the corpus tying the Company Locations Country Code field (or the Company Locations import template) to this list - e.g. a 'use the country codes listed in Country Code List' cross-reference, or the Company Locations import template's column spec (which this corpus never publishes; see the roster's downloadImportTemplateLink gap). Absent that, it stays an unwired catalog. Alternatively it can be wired to a Vendor Manager import field when that page is built - that is its documented home.

valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. valueSets.context: The complete Available VAT Fields table - every field name available when working with VAT at header and line item level
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: 27 rows, complete and in source order, nothing sampled. I checked the existing 30-node configValueSets array: this catalog is NOT yet in the graph, so it is a real gap, not a duplicate.

valueSets.context: The complete Prorated VAT Fields table exposed through the Payment Request Account Extract
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. valueSets.context: The four VAT labels addable to the Payment Request Line Item Details form
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: 4 rows, the complete table. A Forms and Fields configuration (which labels to add to a form), not a Tax Administration control. The source adds a hard rule - 'The admin must add the VAT Type field as part of this configuration' - making VAT Type mandatory whenever these labels are used. NOT HARVESTED, deliberately: the same topic gives Canada's GST / PST as an EXAMPLE of what VAT Type displays, and an example is not an option list. Note the dependency worth recording when that wiring happens: VAT Type's displayed content is the line-item VAT amount fields 1-4, so this catalog and the Available VAT Fields catalog describe the same underlying four-slot structure from two directions.

valueSets.context: Canada FOUR-field VAT labelling convention (tools-guides only)
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: Complete bullet run of 4. A RECOMMENDED LABELLING SCHEME applied on Forms and Fields, not an option list of any Tax Administration control - the values are instructions about what to call a field, not things you select. SOURCE CHARACTER: the separator is an EN DASH (U+2013), not a hyphen. This topic DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the admin-guides claim (supported-countries-for-vat-8b38bab8.md) that Canada is not supported for VAT; both are recorded, neither is reconciled - and note rule 1, this contradiction is only visible if you search tools-guides as hard as admin-guides. The same topic warns that VAT Amount 3 and VAT Amount 4 'must be entered manually at this time' on Capture Processing forms. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A Forms and Fields owner, or a country-implementation-guidance node. It should never become validValues of anything on Tax Administration.

valueSets.context: Canada TWO-field VAT labelling convention - the documented alternative to the four-field scheme
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: Complete bullet run of 2, reproduced as whole clauses because that is how the source writes them - they are sentences of guidance, not selectable values, which is precisely why no field can own them. Chosen by clients operating in a single province, or by clients who prefer VAT Tax Code to distinguish tax types. Under this scheme Capture Processing extracts primary tax to VAT Amount 1 and provincial tax to VAT Amount 2. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Nothing makes these validValues. If they are ever modelled, they belong as guidance attached to the Canada implementation, alongside the four-field scheme, with the two schemes marked as ALTERNATIVES to each other.

valueSets.context: Digital tax invoice (CFDi) validation statuses shown to the processor on hover
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: Complete bullet run of 4. These are RUNTIME STATUS values on a payment request, not a configuration control's options - nothing on Tax Administration (or on any Group 5B page) selects among them. The configuration surface they imply lives elsewhere: workflow steps and audit rules keyed to exception code INVXMLST, i.e. the Audit Rules page (built) and Workflows (not yet built). Feature enablement is by SAP Concur support, not self-service. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Nothing on these four pages. If the graph ever models runtime document states, this is a clean, complete, verbatim set to seed it with; as a config value set it has no legitimate owner.

valueSets.context: Vendor IMPORT TEMPLATE Tax Type codes - the closed list for the vendor record's tax status
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: 3 values, complete, verbatim INCLUDING the source's markdown underscore emphasis around each code and its inconsistent punctuation - DITX and DNTX use an ASCII hyphen, INTX uses an EN DASH (U+2013). Source sentence: 'This is the tax status of the vendor. Select one of the following options:' followed by 'One of the following values only:'. THIS IS A DIFFERENT SURFACE from the Tax Administration vendor group wizard: it is a column of the Vendor Manager import template, owned by a vendor-import page this graph has not built. It is reported here ONLY because it is the nearest closed enumeration to vendorGroupTaxType and someone will be tempted to copy it there. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A Vendor import / Vendor Manager page in the graph. DO NOT wire it to Tax Administration's vendorGroupTaxType - that control's documented options are the open 'international, domestic, taxable, etc.' list, and substituting these codes would fabricate a tenant's screen. The Tax Administration roster gives the same instruction independently.

valueSets.context: The two tabs of the Company Locations page, enumerated together in a single sentence
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: The Company Locations roster models the tabs as TWO separate fields, shipToTab and billToTab, so there is no single tab-selector field for this pair to attach to; the extraction lens's proposed owner 'companyLocationTab' is not a roster field name and inventing it now would violate the roster's authority. Worth keeping as a candidate because this really is an enumerated pair from ONE documented sentence (not a completed toggle) and it recurs verbatim in export-shipping-or-billing-addresses-59f051b2.md. LABEL DRIFT that any automation must survive: the tabs are 'Ship To' / 'Bill To', but the windows they open are 'Add New Ship To Location', 'Modify Ship To Location' and 'Import Ship To Locations', while prose elsewhere writes 'ship-to' / 'bill-to' and 'Ship-To' / 'Bill-To'. The corpus never shows an 'Add New Bill To Location' window title, and the tabs are NOT field-identical - VAT ID is documented as bill-to only. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: A single tab-selector field on the Company Locations roster, following the graph's existing convention for tab groups (capture_processing_admin_tabs on Capture Processing Admin). That is a roster change - a field addition - which this pass is explicitly forbidden to make, so it is reported instead.

valueSets.context: 'New List Category' - the create-a-category branch of the List Management New List page category control
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. WHY NO OWNER: DO NOT WIRE THIS. It is recorded only so the decision is auditable. extract-list-management-tables.json emitted it as a value set against 'listCategorySelector', which is not a roster field name; the obvious rewire target is the roster field listCategory. The List Management roster explicitly forbids that rewire and instructs the merger to DROP the set outright, because the corpus never states that the New List Category entry lives INSIDE the category control - the only sentence is 'Create New: Select New List Category and, in Add New List Category, type a name and select Save.', and 'Select' establishes neither a widget nor a membership. That membership is plausible, and plausible is exactly the class of completion this project has already deleted twice. The roster instead models the string once, as its own field newListCategoryOption with empty validValues, and marks the question UNDETERMINED. 'Allocations' is likewise excluded everywhere: the corpus offers it as an example of an existing category ('such as Allocations'), i.e. tenant data. If that is ever found, the roster's own instruction applies: the string moves into listCategory.validValues and the newListCategoryOption field is REMOVED, so the string is never counted twice. valueSets.context: 'Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code' - the ten segment levels a List Management source list can carry downstream (COMPRESSED RANGE kept in the source's own form)
valueSets.notes: ACCEPTED GAP - deliberately unwired. The expansion above is the ten names. These are COLUMNS OF AN IMPORT TEMPLATE, not options of any List Management control: the nearest List Management field is addSubLevels ('continue to add sub-levels as required'), which is a mechanism, not a chooser, and which the corpus never gives a depth limit. Wiring ten import column names as that control's values would misrepresent the page. The identical ten columns appear UNCOMPRESSED, one row each, in two other topics - tools-guides/the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md and admin-guides/import-settings-record-type-200-format-c244e3ab.md - all ten rows of both were read; none sampled. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Either an import-template page in the graph to own the columns, or a documented depth limit on List Management itself, which would make ten a page-level constraint rather than a downstream one. As it stands this range is the ONLY documented bound on how deep a List Management source list is carried downstream, which is why it is preserved here rather than dropped.

dependencies.condition: The Country (and State/Province) chosen on the Tax Authorities tab is not evaluated in isolation: the system resolves it against the ship-to addresses maintained on the Company Locations Ship To tab to decide whether a transaction is domestic or foreign and therefore which authority/rate applies. Company Locations must hold ship-to rows for a tax authority to resolve.
dependencies.sourceQuote: When the admin selects Country and State/Province in the Tax Authorities tab, Invoice will pull the ship-to information from the Company Locations page in Administration

dependencies.condition: The state/province recorded on the ship-to address changes the VAT calculation, so the State/Province value set on the tax authority only has effect in combination with the matching State/Province on the Company Locations address. INFERRED endpoint pairing: the quoted sentence is about the ship-to location's state or province and does not name either field control by its on-screen label; the two named endpoints are the fields that carry that value on each page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In addition, the specific state or province may alter the calculation as well.

dependencies.condition: The documented calculation identity makes a tax authority inert on its own: VAT is computed from the three-part product of tax authority, company location (Ship To) and expense type or vendor. A tax authority configured with no matching Company Location produces no calculation.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Tax Authority + Company Location (Ship To) + Expense Type (or Vendor) = Calculation

dependencies.condition: Stated as a hard requirement of the Tax Validation feature: a Ship To value must already exist in Company Locations (and be selected on the employee profile) for tax validation to work, so Company Locations is populated before Tax Validation is switched on.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Tax Validation feature requires that a Ship To value specified in Company Locations be selected in the employee’s Profile > Invoice Preferences > Default Shipping Address field.

dependencies.condition: Explicit ordering statement in the basic process for the Tax Authority feature: VAT fields are added to the relevant forms in Forms and Fields BEFORE any tax authority is configured.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Clients need to add VAT fields to the relevant forms before they start configuring the Tax Authority feature.

dependencies.condition: Hard capability limit that constrains which Forms and Fields VAT fields a tax authority can drive: only the first VAT amount field triple is supported. Adding VAT Amount 2/3/4 fields on a form does not extend Tax Authority coverage.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Currently, in Tax Authority, Concur Invoice only supports one VAT amount field (VAT Amount 1/VAT Rate 1/VAT Tax Code 1).

dependencies.condition: The Rate Type option list on the expense type group's Tax Rates step is not free entry - it is scoped to, and populated from, the Tax Rate Type Name values already created for the selected tax authority in the New Tax Authority wizard. Rate types must exist on the authority first.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To change the rate type, click the field in the Rate Type column to select from the list, which displays the rate types available for the selected tax authority.

dependencies.condition: Vendor-group twin of the expense-type-group rule: the Rate Type column on the vendor group Tax Rates step offers only the rate types defined for the selected tax authority. Republished sentence in the Step 6 topic, so it is corroboration on a different wizard, not a duplicate of one statement.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To change the rate type, click the field in the Rate Type column to select from the list, which displays the rate types available for the selected tax authority.

dependencies.condition: The Expense Types Group tab begins by selecting an existing tax authority from a list, so a tax authority must be created in the New Tax Authority wizard before any expense type group can be added. INFERRED only in that the corpus does not restate that the list is populated from taxAuthorityName; the ordering itself is documented as step 1 of the Group Name step.
dependencies.sourceQuote: On the Expense Types Group tab, select from the Tax Authority list.

dependencies.condition: Vendor-group twin: the Vendor Groups tab likewise starts from a Tax Authority selection, so the authority must exist first.
dependencies.sourceQuote: On the Vendor Groups tab, select from the Tax Authority list.

dependencies.condition: The group grid returned by Search is scoped by the Tax Authority selected in the filter above it - the search returns the existing groups for that authority only, not all groups on the page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The existing groups for the selected tax authority, if any, appear.

dependencies.condition: One-group-per-tax-authority exclusivity: an expense type consumed by an existing group under the same tax authority is not selectable for a new group - it is shown instead in the read-only Unavailable Expense Types pane, annotated with the group that holds it. The selectable set therefore depends on what earlier groups already took.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Any expense types that are already used for this tax authority appear in the Unavailable Expense Types pane with the name of the group.

dependencies.condition: Vendor twin of the exclusivity rule, and the reason the pane's contents change with the authority: which vendors are shown as unavailable is scoped to the tax authority selected for the group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Any vendors that are already used for this tax authority appear in the Unavailable Vendors pane with the name of the group.

dependencies.condition: End Date is not independent - it closes the range opened by Effective Date, and is optional. Left blank the system substitutes 12/31/9999 ('If no end date is specified, the system uses the date of 12/31/9999', understand-and-use-the-effective-date-and-the-end-date-ccf72f26.md), so groups are chained by date rather than deleted.
dependencies.sourceQuote: (Optional) Select the end date for the group's effective date range.

dependencies.condition: The Disable VAT calculation check box is only honoured for the invoice document type, so its effect is conditioned by the Applies To document type selected for the group. The corpus names only 'Payment Request' as an Applies To document type and does not enumerate an option list.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You can only disable VAT calculation for invoices.

dependencies.condition: Cross-tab consistency constraint: the VAT calculation mode chosen on the vendor group tab must agree with the one chosen on the expense type group tab. The two group wizards cannot be configured independently. The docs give the worked example 'if you select line item in the expense type group configuration, you should also select line item as a VAT calculation mode.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Ensure that you are consistent if you configure expense type groups or vendor groups and define the VAT calculation mode.

dependencies.condition: Expense type groups are assembled from the tenant's own configured expense types, and the expense type is one of the three inputs to the calculation - so the expense types must exist on the Expense Types page before a group can select them.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The unique combination of tax authority, company location, and expense type is used to calculate the tax.

dependencies.condition: The Expense Types column on the Tax Validation tab is a read-only rendering of the tenant's client-defined expense types; nothing can be added or renamed here, only mapped to a commodity code. Its contents are wholly determined by the Expense Types page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This list of expense types represents the client-defined expense types.

dependencies.condition: The expense-type-to-commodity-code mapping has two documented population paths - in-grid manual entry on this tab, or the Expense Type import - so an automation driving this grid must know whether the import already owns the mapping. Target field is the Expense Type import's key column; the corpus does not name a commodity-code column in the Expense Type import template.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This is done by either manually entering the proper code, or by using the Expense Type import.

dependencies.condition: Explicit sequencing warning: the commodity-code mapping (and every other configuration step) must be finished before the activation check box is selected. Corroborated by the-basic-process-13c136d5.md: 'The feature is not active until the client selects (enables) the Turn On Tax Validation check box in the Tax Administration tool.'
dependencies.sourceQuote: Do not activate the service until all configuration steps, such as expense type to commodity code mapping, are finalized.

dependencies.condition: The activation check box is scoped, not global: it turns validation on for whichever request type is selected in Tax Validation Type. That control has exactly one documented value, Payment Request Only.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) to activate tax validation for the specified request type.

dependencies.condition: Predefining tax codes on the Tax Code tab is what converts the end user's VAT tax code fields from read-only text into selectable lists; without predefined codes they stay read-only. CORPUS CONTRADICTION on scope: configure-predefined-tax-codes-6b42509f.md says the user sees 'the tax code fields (1-4) as a list', while step-7-optional-configure-predefined-tax-codes-be8bc5b8.md says the user sees 'the VAT Tax Code 1 field as a list'. Both are recorded; neither is reconciled.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If the admin does not predefine tax codes, the user will see the tax codes in read-only fields and not in lists.

dependencies.condition: Predefining a tax code is necessary but not sufficient for the user to change it: modify rights on the VAT tax code fields are granted separately in Forms and Fields.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To edit the VAT tax code fields, the admin needs to ensure the user has been given modify rights of these fields in the Forms and Fields tool.

dependencies.condition: A tax authority silently overwrites values that Capture Processing extracted: when the captured VAT Amount 1 field (header or line item) is auto-updated by tax-authority-driven recalculation, an Audit Trail entry is written. Corroborated in tools-guides: 'an audit trail entry is created whenever the tax and VAT data changes due to processing and final assignments as described above.' (working-with-tax-and-vat-data-f690215c.md)
dependencies.sourceQuote: Whenever the Capture Processing VAT Amount 1 (header or line item) field, entered during Invoice Capture, is auto-updated by Tax Authority-based changes, the system will log a value in the Audit Trail of the invoice

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - the vendor master page is not built in this graph. Vendor records must exist before vendor groups can be assembled on the Vendor Groups tab. Related contradiction worth carrying: the Vendor Import template enumerates its OWN Tax Type list (DITX/DNTX/INTX) for vendor records (tools-guides/the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b53850b.md) - that is a different control on a different surface and must never be copied onto the Tax Administration vendorGroupTaxType field, whose corpus wording ('international, domestic, taxable, etc.') is open-ended prose.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Vendor information is needed when vendor groups are configured for Tax Authority

dependencies.condition: A policy's Bill To value is chosen from addresses that already exist in Company Locations, and the string offered is the address Name. The address must be created here before the policy can reference it. Corroborated: 'Be sure to type in the name of the location whenever you are asked for a Bill To or Ship To address you create by using Company Locations.' (same file)
dependencies.sourceQuote: This is the value that displays when choosing a default shipping address in Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Preferences, and when creating a policy and selecting the value for Bill To.

dependencies.condition: Two-sided precondition: the Use Email as Bill-To field on the Purchase Order Header form does nothing unless BOTH the field has been added in Forms and Fields AND an email address has been entered on the bill-to record in Company Locations. Adding the field alone is not enough.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Provided the admin has added the Use Email as Bill-To field to the Purchase Order Header form in the Forms and Fields tool and entered an email address in the bill-to email address field in the Company Locations tool

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - Peppol Configuration is not yet built. Hard integration constraint with a failure mode named in the docs: the ship-to Address Code held here must match the code on inbound Peppol invoices, or invoice creation fails outright.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The company ship-to address code maintained in Company Locations in Concur Invoice must match the ship-to address code in the invoices coming from Peppol. If the address codes don't match, invoice creation fails.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - no page node exists for the Purchase Order import (record types 210 bill-to and 220 ship-to). Identity claim: the on-page Address Code and the import's External ID are the same identifier, so an automation must not allocate them independently.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - no Purchase Order import page node. Distinct claim from the identity edge above: a PO import record carrying a matching pair UPDATES the existing Company Locations address row rather than creating a second one, so the import can silently rewrite rows a crawler just created.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Identical records are those that share the same Address Code (in Company Locations) and External ID (within the associated record in the PO import).

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - the Employee Import (360-level record set) has no page node in this graph. A user's default shipping address is assigned by quoting the Address Code of an address that must already exist in Company Locations. The admin-side twin of the same rule: 'This field uses the unique location code provided by the client that identifies the default shipping address associated with the imported user' (admin-guides/set-a-default-shipping-and-billing-address-f772bed1.md).
dependencies.sourceQuote: To assign a user's preferred shipping address, use the 360-record set (Invoice Employee Import) in the Employee Import. Specify the Address Code of the preferred address.

dependencies.condition: Selecting this check box while entering a bill-to address causes a ship-to record to be populated with the same address information - one action writes rows on both tabs. The corpus does not resolve why the check box is documented inside a table introduced under the Ship To tab.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select (enable) this check box if you would like to populate the ship-to address with the same address information as the bill-to address.

dependencies.condition: The one row that makes the two tabs' field sets non-identical: VAT ID applies only on the bill-to side, and is required in some European countries. The corpus does not say which countries.
dependencies.sourceQuote: This is only applicable on the bill-to address and required by some European countries.

dependencies.condition: The accepted format of Country Code depends on the entry path: the 2-character ISO code is mandated only for the import template. The corpus never enumerates the accepted values for the on-page control, and the 249-row Country Code List catalog in the corpus is documented for the vendor import file, a different scope.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If you are using the import template to import company locations, you must use 2 character ISO code.

dependencies.condition: Remove is a soft delete keyed on Address Code: the removed address stays available to existing requests, and re-entering the same Address Code reactivates it - but as a NEW record, not the original. An automation that re-creates a removed code will not restore the old row.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The address remains available and can be reactivated by entering the same Address Code. The system creates a new record.

dependencies.condition: The strongest cross-page statement on this page: creating the source list here IS creating the groups that Group Configurations then configures, because each list item is in effect a group. Group Configurations cannot originate a group.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The process of creating this list is equivalent to creating Groups since each item in the source list is in effect a group.

dependencies.condition: The named groups set up in Group Configurations must correspond one-for-one to the source list items created first in List Management - the worked example adds four Divisions matching the four list items.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In the following figure, four Divisions are added that match the source list items created in Step 1.

dependencies.condition: A group cannot be deleted from Group Configurations at all - deletion is performed by removing the corresponding item from the source list on List Management. The Group Configurations delete control does not reach group identity.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To delete a group, remove the corresponding item from the Source List.

dependencies.condition: Page boundary between the two tools: the list itself (category, list, items) is built on List Management, and the connected list DEFINITION on the Forms and Fields Connected Lists tab then selects that already-created list.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The connected list created in List Management is chosen when defining the connected list for addition to the Payment Request Quantified Line Items form in Step 2

dependencies.condition: Documented task ordering across the two pages: fields are added to forms on Forms and Fields, then the lists needed for the invoice forms are identified and created on List Management ('Identify and create the lists needed for the invoice forms.'), then field properties are modified back on Forms and Fields to substitute a list for a text box. INFERRED in part: the corpus gives an ordered task list rather than stating this pairwise dependency in one sentence.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You use the Forms and Fields and List Management pages to perform the following tasks, typically in the order shown.

dependencies.condition: Hard display cap that bounds how large a List Management list can usefully be: a field configured as a simple list renders at most 500 items. Above that the field degrades on the form, not on this page.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a field is configured as a simple list, the field displays a maximum of 500 items in the list:

dependencies.condition: Connected-list counterpart of the 500-item cap: a connected list shows at most 500 items and lets the user search by either the list item text or its code, so the number of items created in List Management bounds what the form can render. Retargeted to itemName (the displayed text) to keep it distinct from the separate single-use constraint on itemCode.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a field is defined as a connected list, it will display a maximum of 500 items in the connected list, and it will allow the user to search either by the list item text or code:

dependencies.condition: The Connected Lists tab is the route for a list that was built with sub-levels in List Management; a single-level list does not need it. Which tab to use on Forms and Fields depends on whether sub-levels were added here.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Use the Connected Lists tab if you have created a multi-level vendor group list

dependencies.condition: When an expense type is used as the first field of a connected list, the Item Code entered here must EXACTLY match the code of that expense type. The expense type must therefore already exist and its code be known.
dependencies.sourceQuote: with an Item Code that _exactly_ matches that of the expense type you are using (example: Awards = "AWRDS")

dependencies.condition: Conditional naming constraint, distinct from the Item Code rule: Item Name must match the Expense Type name exactly ONLY if the name is required to appear the same in connected list audit rules. The condition is inside the source sentence and must not be dropped.
dependencies.sourceQuote: be sure the value you input for Item Name matches the Expense Type name exactly.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - Localization is not yet built. To learn the Item Code values that must be matched for SYSTEM expense types, the admin exports them from the Localization page (or runs a Cognos report); the codes are not discoverable from List Management or Expense Types.
dependencies.sourceQuote: To find the Item Code values, run a report from Cognos or export a list of system expense types by using the Localization page in Administration.

dependencies.condition: Ordering constraint enforced in the connected list definition, on items created here: the Expense Type List Item Key field must be FIRST in the connected list or the expense-type-as-first-field feature does not work.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Expense Type List Item Key field must be the first item in the connected list for this feature to work.

dependencies.condition: SECOND, DISTINCT CONSTRAINT on the same pair, gating a different decision than the ordering rule: the Expense Type List Item Key field is single-use. Once one connected list definition consumes it, it is no longer offered - so which list gets it must be decided before any list is defined.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The Expense Type List Item Key field can only be used in a single connected list definition, after which it is no longer available.

dependencies.condition: The ten Level n Code columns of the hierarchy-mapping import template consumed by Routing Configuration ARE the List Management list item short codes, so the import file cannot be authored until the list items exist and their codes are recorded. Corroborated on the admin side: 'The list item Short Code representing the 1st segment level of the overall hierarchy path.' (admin-guides/import-settings-record-type-200-format-c244e3ab.md). COMPRESSED RANGE: Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code expands to ten columns; List Management itself is given no documented depth limit.
dependencies.sourceQuote: These are the List Item Short Codes.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - Feature Hierarchies is not yet built. The list created and named here in Step 1 is the exact list selected as the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy's Source List in Step 2.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - Feature Hierarchies is not yet built. Cardinality rule: a multi-level source list forces matching additional levels and segments on the feature hierarchy, so the number of sub-levels added here determines the hierarchy's shape.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - no page node for the Vendor Employee Access import. Exact-match rule on the codes recorded here: the import file must reproduce them character for character. Corroborated on the template side: 'Level 1 of the source list attached to the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy.' (tools-guides/the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md).
dependencies.sourceQuote: The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE - no page node for Invoice Pay check configurations / funding accounts; the corpus attributes their setup to the external Concur Invoice: Invoice Pay Setup Guide. The payment groups those configurations batch on are items in a List Management list, surfaced on the invoice header as a drop-down, so the list items bound the available payment groups.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Payments Groups are linked to items in a list from List Management and selected on an invoice from a drop-down list field in the Invoice Details (Header) section.

dependencies.condition: Internal two-stage ordering that a crawler must respect: the list must be created and saved first, then selected, before the second New button (which adds list ITEMS, not a list) is available. The two New buttons look identical on screen.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the list name, and then click New to begin creating the list items

dependencies.condition: A list is created inside a category: on the New List page the admin either selects an existing list category or creates one via New List Category, and both the category name and the list name are then required by the list import. INFERRED ordering: the corpus documents the category choice as an earlier numbered step than the page Save, but never states the ordering as a rule. The corpus enumerates NO list categories - 'such as Allocations' is a single illustrative example.
dependencies.sourceQuote: When you define the list, make note of the category name and the list name; you will need them for the list import.

dependencies.condition: The contents of the Unavailable Expense Types pane are determined by the tax authority selected for the group: expense types already consumed by that authority appear there, annotated with the owning group, and cannot be selected again. Added 2026-08-31 from the Group 5B correctness critic to mirror the vendor-group edge, which the same sentence in step-6 already produced; without it the expense-type side of an identical rule was unmodelled.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Any expense types that are already used for this tax authority appear in the Unavailable Expense Types pane with the name of the group

dependencies.condition: The Tax Percent field is not present on the Tax Rates step until a Rate Type has been selected - a conditional field appearance, not merely a disabled control. A crawler that looks for Tax Percent before setting Rate Type will not find it. Added 2026-08-31 from the Group 5B correctness critic.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Once you select the type, the Tax Percent field appears.

steps.name: Stand up a tax authority end to end (VAT fields, ship-to data, authority, rate types, rates)
steps.goal: A tax authority (usually a country) exists on the Tax Authorities tab with at least one tax rate type and one dated rate, AND the VAT it calculates has somewhere to land and something to resolve against.
